protocols.name: The day arc
protocols.notes: Four anchors: before you get up, while the kettle boils, before bed, and in bed. Each one has a sixty-second version that counts — miss the long one and the floor is still the whole thing.

blocks.name: Before your feet touch the floor

items.name: Rocking child’s pose
items.why: The floor version. Sixty seconds of rocking is the whole block on a bad morning.

fields.tool: Your bed, before you get up.
fields.release: Knees under you, sit back toward your heels, arms forward. Rock slowly forward and back — small, unhurried, breathing out longer than you breathe in.
fields.notice: The low back lets go first, then the hips. The breath drops out of the chest.
fields.careful: Knees that object get a pillow behind them, or do this on your side instead. Nothing here is worth pain first thing.

items.name: Lean-forward lat and shoulder stretch
items.why: A night on one side shortens what you slept on. This reverses it before you stand up on it.

fields.release: From the same kneeling position, walk both hands to one side until you feel the stretch down the outside of the ribs and into the armpit. Breathe into that side. Then the other side.
fields.notice: Ribs move on that side again. The overhead reach feels less blocked.
fields.careful: If a shoulder feels unstable overhead, keep the elbow bent and stay short of the end range.

items.name: Kneel-sit chest opener
items.why: Undoes the curl the night put in — chest, front of shoulders, hip flexors, all at once.

fields.release: Sit back on your heels, hands behind you on the bed, fingers pointing away. Lift the chest and let the shoulders roll back. Breathe wide, not deep.
fields.notice: The first full breath of the day usually arrives here.
fields.careful: Wrists that complain: make fists and rest on the knuckles, or drop to the forearms.

items.name: Forward fold, hanging
items.why: The floor version. One minute while something else is happening.

fields.tool: Whatever you already do first — coffee brewing, the shower warming up.
fields.release: Feet hip-width, knees soft — never locked back. Fold and hang. Let the head go. Sway a little if it helps.
fields.notice: The hamstrings stop arguing after about thirty seconds. That is the point where it starts working.
fields.careful: Soft knees, always. Locking them to reach further is the exact thing this is undoing.

items.name: Hip circles
items.why: The hips have not moved through their own range in eight hours.

fields.release: Hands on hips, feet planted. Draw the biggest slow circle you can with the pelvis, one way then the other. Keep the ribs still — this is the hips moving, not the whole torso.
fields.notice: One direction is always worse than the other. That is information, not a fault.

items.name: Horse stance, rocks and shifts
items.why: Wakes up the deep hip and pelvic-floor work that standing all day never asks for.

fields.release: Wide stance, toes slightly out, sit down into a quarter squat. Rock the pelvis front to back, then shift your weight side to side. Slow.
fields.notice: The inner thighs and the floor of the pelvis switch on. Standing feels more planted afterwards.
fields.careful: Knees track over the toes, not inside them. Go shallow — depth is not what this is for.

items.name: Extended exhale
items.why: The floor version, and the one that does the most for the least.

fields.release: Breathe in through the nose for four, out through the nose for eight. Sixty seconds. The out-breath is the whole mechanism — long and unforced.
fields.notice: Shoulders drop without being told to. The body decides it is safe to downshift.
fields.careful: Lightheaded means shorten it, not push. This should feel like less effort, not more.

items.name: Deep release, wherever today landed
items.why: The day’s worst offender gets the pressure. Melting into the floor is the signal it worked — that is the nervous system letting go, not the tissue.

fields.tool: A firm ball, a roller, or your own hands.
fields.release: Pick what actually bothered you today rather than a routine. Sink in and wait — sixty to ninety seconds a spot. Breathe out through the intensity instead of holding your breath against it.
fields.load: Follow it with something that uses the range you just opened, even briefly. Range you do not load is range you give back overnight.
fields.notice: The sink-into-the-floor feeling. Breathing gets easier while you are still on the spot.
fields.careful: Sharp pain, numbness or anything shooting down a limb means move off it — that is nerve, not muscle, and pressure is the wrong answer.

items.name: Supine knee rocks
items.why: The floor version. One minute of this is a complete evening block.

fields.release: On your back, knees bent, feet down. Let both knees fall slowly to one side, then the other. Rhythmic and small. No effort at all.
fields.notice: The low back unwinds. Most people stop noticing they are doing it, which is the idea.

items.name: Prone bent-knee foot swings
items.why: A rhythmic motion that carries people into sleep — the point is the rhythm, not the stretch.

fields.release: Face down, knees bent, ankles crossed or apart. Swing the feet slowly side to side like a metronome. Let it get boring.
fields.notice: Breathing slows on its own. Stopping because you drifted off is a success, not a skipped item.
fields.careful: Face down is not for everyone — if the low back complains, stay on your back and keep rocking the knees instead.

protocols.name: Morning and evening flow
protocols.notes: Two short routines, ten minutes each. Edit anything — it is yours now.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.why: 8 slow breaths

fields.release: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips. INHALE: Drop belly toward floor, lift chest and tailbone (Cow). EXHALE: Round spine toward ceiling, tuck chin and pelvis (Cat). Move slowly with breath, feeling each vertebra articulate.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: spine, core.

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.why: 20 sec each side

fields.release: From hands and knees, reach right arm under your left arm, sliding it along the floor. Let your right shoulder and temple rest on the ground. Hold, breathing into the stretch. Return and repeat on the other side.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: thoracic spine, shoulders.

items.name: World's Greatest Stretch
items.why: 5 per side with rotation

fields.release: Step right foot outside right hand in a deep lunge. Drop left knee (optional). Rotate right arm to the sky, opening chest. Hold, then bring elbow toward the floor inside the right foot. Straighten front leg for hamstring stretch. Repeat other side.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hip flexors, hamstrings, thoracic spine, groin.

items.name: Downward Dog
items.why: Pedal feet, press heels

fields.release: From hands and knees, tuck toes, lift hips high and back. Press chest toward thighs, heels toward floor (they don't need to touch). Spread fingers wide, externally rotate upper arms. Pedal feet to warm up calves and hamstrings.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hamstrings, calves, shoulders, spine.

items.name: Standing Hamstring Stretch
items.why: 20 sec each leg

fields.release: Place one foot on a low step or bench (or just extend in front of you). Keep the elevated leg straight. Hinge at the hips and lean forward with a flat back until you feel the stretch behind the thigh. Keep hips square. Hold and switch.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hamstrings, calves.

items.name: Hip CARs
items.why: 3 slow circles each leg

fields.release: Controlled Articular Rotations. Stand on one leg (hold wall if needed). Lift knee to chest, rotate it out to the side, extend behind you, then reverse. Move SLOWLY through the biggest circle you can control. This maps your hip's full range of motion.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hips, hip flexors, glutes.

items.name: Deep Squat Hold
items.why: Shift weight side to side

fields.release: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulders, toes slightly out. Sink hips down as low as possible while keeping heels on the floor. Use elbows to push knees outward. Keep chest up. If heels lift, widen stance or hold something for balance.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hips, ankles, quads, adductors.

items.name: Ankle CARs
items.why: 5 circles each foot

fields.release: Controlled Articular Rotations for ankles. Lift one foot off the ground. Slowly draw the largest circle you can with your toes, moving only at the ankle joint. Go clockwise, then counterclockwise. Keep the rest of your leg still.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: ankles, calves, tibialis.

items.name: Shoulder CARs
items.why: 3 slow circles each arm

fields.release: Stand tall, arm at your side. Slowly raise arm forward, overhead, behind you, and back down in the biggest circle you can control. Keep your torso completely still — only the shoulder moves. Reverse direction.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: shoulders, rotator cuff.

items.name: Lateral Lunge Hold
items.why: 20 sec each side

fields.release: Step wide to the right, bending right knee and pushing hips back while keeping left leg straight. Keep both feet flat. Sit into the bent knee side. Feel the stretch in the straight leg's inner thigh. Hold, then switch sides.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: adductors, groin, hamstrings, quads.

items.name: Doorway Chest Stretch
items.why: Open the chest, shoulders back

fields.release: Stand in a doorway. Place forearms on the door frame at 90° (elbows at shoulder height). Step one foot through and lean forward until you feel the stretch across your chest. Adjust arm height to target different pec fibers — higher hits upper chest, lower hits lower.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: chest, anterior deltoids.

items.name: Neck Stretch
items.why: Side, diagonal, and front

fields.release: Sit or stand tall. Tilt right ear toward right shoulder. Gently place right hand on top of head for light overpressure. Keep left shoulder down. Hold 15-20 seconds. For the front of the neck, look up and slightly to one side. Switch sides.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: neck, upper traps.

items.name: Child's Pose
items.why: Wide knees, walk hands L/R for lat stretch

fields.release: Kneel on the floor, big toes together, knees wide. Sit hips back toward heels and walk hands forward, lowering chest toward floor. Rest forehead on the ground. For lat stretch, walk both hands to one side and hold, then switch.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: back, hips, lats.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.why: Segmental, match breath

fields.release: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips. INHALE: Drop belly toward floor, lift chest and tailbone (Cow). EXHALE: Round spine toward ceiling, tuck chin and pelvis (Cat). Move slowly with breath, feeling each vertebra articulate.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: spine, core.

items.name: Thread the Needle
items.why: 20 sec each side, sink into it

fields.release: From hands and knees, reach right arm under your left arm, sliding it along the floor. Let your right shoulder and temple rest on the ground. Hold, breathing into the stretch. Return and repeat on the other side.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: thoracic spine, shoulders.

items.name: Pigeon Stretch
items.why: 30 sec each side, melt forward

fields.release: From downward dog, bring right knee forward behind right wrist. Extend left leg straight behind you. Square your hips. Upright pigeon: stay on hands. Sleeping pigeon: fold forward over front leg. Hold and breathe. Switch sides.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: glutes, hip flexors, piriformis.

items.name: Supine Figure-4 Stretch
items.why: 20 sec each side

fields.release: Lie on your back. Cross right ankle over left knee (making a "4" shape). Reach through and pull the left thigh toward your chest. You should feel a deep stretch in the right glute/hip. Keep head on the floor. Hold and switch.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: glutes, piriformis, hips.

items.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
items.why: 25 sec each leg

fields.release: Lie on your back. Lift one leg and hold behind the thigh or calf (use a towel or strap if needed). Keep the leg as straight as possible. Keep the other leg flat on the floor. Pull gently to deepen the stretch. Hold and breathe.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hamstrings.

items.name: Supine Spinal Twist
items.why: 25 sec each side

fields.release: Lie on your back, arms in a T. Pull one knee to chest, then guide it across your body to the opposite side. Let gravity pull the knee toward the floor. Keep both shoulders pressed down. Look in the opposite direction of the knee. Breathe and melt into it.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: spine, obliques, glutes, chest.

items.name: Butterfly Stretch
items.why: Feet together, knees out, fold forward

fields.release: Sit with soles of feet together, knees falling outward. Hold feet and sit tall. Gently press knees toward floor with elbows or let gravity work. For deeper stretch, fold forward from the hips while maintaining a long spine.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: adductors, groin, hips.

items.name: Neck Stretch
items.why: Gentle, just gravity

fields.release: Sit or stand tall. Tilt right ear toward right shoulder. Gently place right hand on top of head for light overpressure. Keep left shoulder down. Hold 15-20 seconds. For the front of the neck, look up and slightly to one side. Switch sides.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: neck, upper traps.

items.name: Legs Up the Wall
items.why: Close eyes, deep breaths

fields.release: Sit with one hip against a wall, then swing your legs up as you lie back. Scoot your butt as close to the wall as comfortable. Arms at sides or on belly. Close your eyes. This inverts blood flow, calms the nervous system, and gently stretches hamstrings.
fields.notice: Where you should feel it: hamstrings, lower back, nervous system.

protocols.name: Daily support
protocols.notes: Movement, drainage and downregulation — the practices that are not a routine and not a supplement. The occasional ones are marked "when needed": present, never late.

items.name: Movement 20–30 min
items.why: Lymph needs muscle movement — walk, bike, play, anything counts

items.name: Stretch/yoga 10+ min
items.why: Circulation + stress reduction

items.name: Strength training
items.why: Build muscle, support metabolism, improve bone density

items.name: Castor oil pack
items.why: Liver area, 30–60 min with heat — supports detox and inflammation

items.name: Sweat session
items.why: Skin = detox organ — sauna, hot bath, or intense exercise

items.name: Cold exposure
items.why: Cold shower or plunge — reduces inflammation, boosts dopamine, builds resilience

items.name: Dry brushing
items.why: Stimulates lymphatic drainage, exfoliates skin, improves circulation

items.name: Coffee enema
items.why: Liver/gallbladder support — follow practitioner guidance

items.name: Oil pulling
items.why: Swish coconut oil 10–20 min — oral microbiome support

items.name: Cupping
items.why: Increases blood flow, releases fascial tension, supports detox pathways

items.name: Acupressure / acupuncture
items.why: Stimulates meridian points — relieves pain, supports organ function, reduces stress

items.name: Deep breathing 5 min
items.why: Parasympathetic activation — calms fight-or-flight

items.name: Meditation
items.why: Even 5 minutes reduces cortisol and improves focus

items.name: Gratitude / journaling
items.why: Mental clarity, emotional processing, stress reduction

items.name: Morning sunlight 10 min
items.why: Sets circadian rhythm, boosts vitamin D, improves sleep

items.name: Screen-free wind-down
items.why: No screens 30–60 min before bed — protects melatonin production

protocols.name: Body work
protocols.notes: Release paired with the loading that keeps it, plus breathing, airway, nerve glides, balance and downregulation. Each card says how often it comes round; nothing here is daily unless it says so.

items.name: Front of hip
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Lie face down, ball at the front-outside of the hip just inside the hip bone. Sink onto it slowly. Wait for the guard to let go, then a little more. 60–90 sec. Start with the tighter side; the other side lighter.
fields.load: Glute bridge ×10 slow, squeeze at the top. Then standing hip extension ×10 each side. The flexor let go; the glute has to take the job.
fields.notice: Knee-to-chest goes further with less pinch. Clicking quiets. Relaxation runs down the leg.
fields.careful: If a hip clicks, catches or feels like it slides, release is the opener and stability is the fix — do not chase depth.

photos.caption: Half-kneeling hip flexor — the safer swap for the kneeling lean-back the card warns about. Tuck the pelvis under.
The load. Slow, squeeze at the top. The flexor let go; the glute has to take the job.

items.name: Glute & back of hip
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Sit on the floor, ball under one glute, that ankle crossed over the opposite knee. Roll slowly to find the tender spot, then stop and let the pressure build. 60–90 sec each side.
fields.load: Side-lying clamshells ×12 each side, or standing banded abduction. Light band — this is about finding the muscle, not loading it.
fields.notice: Hips sit more level. Less low-back ache when standing.
fields.careful: Deep glute work can catch the sciatic nerve. Numbness or shooting down the leg means move the ball, not push harder.

photos.caption: Ball or roller under one glute, that ankle crossed over the opposite knee. Roll to the tender spot, then stop and let the pressure build.
Further round the side, if the tenderness sits on the outer hip rather than deep in the glute.
A harder bridge once the two-leg version is easy. Light band optional — this is about finding the muscle.

items.name: Feet
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.tool: Firm lacrosse ball, or a golf ball for finer work
fields.release: Ball under the arch — seated first, standing when you want more. Roll the whole sole slowly: heel, arch, ball of foot. Then park on the tender spots. 60–90 sec per foot.
fields.load: Short foot — gently dome the arch without curling the toes, hold 5 sec ×10. Then barefoot balance, eyes open, 30 sec per side.
fields.notice: The ground feels more detailed. Balance steadier. Calves loosen without being touched.
fields.careful: Tender because they're deconditioned, not damaged. Daily and light beats hard and occasional.

photos.caption: Ball under the arch, seated first. Roll heel, arch, ball of foot slowly, then park on the tender spots.

items.name: Calves
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: On the mid-belly of the calf — not the Achilles, not the shin bone. While compressed, slowly point and flex the foot 8–10×. Work the tighter side first.
fields.load: Bilateral heel raises ×15 slow, then lower on the weaker side alone ×8. Add seated bent-knee raises for the soleus.
fields.notice: Knee-to-wall distance improves on the side you worked. The ankle feels like it has more to give.
fields.careful: If either calf has been operated on or injured, release that side lightly or skip it. A weak calf needs strength, not length.

photos.caption: On the mid-belly of the calf. Not the Achilles, not the shin bone. Right side primary; the left is the weak one.

items.name: Hamstrings
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Under the hamstring, seated on the floor with the leg out. Slow. Once you're on a spot, straighten and bend the knee a few times under the pressure.
fields.load: Glute bridge with the feet further out ×10. Then a bodyweight hip hinge with soft knees ×10 — slow, back flat.
fields.notice: The forward fold goes further with the knees soft.
fields.careful: Chase the fold with knees in soft neutral, never locked back. Range here is a fair target; knee hyperextension is not.

photos.caption: Under the hamstring, seated, leg out. Once you are on a spot, bend and straighten the knee under the pressure.
The load. Bridge with the feet further out than usual.

items.name: Chest & front of shoulder
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Ball between your chest and a wall, just below and inside the front of the shoulder — the meaty part near the armpit, not on bone. Lean in, then slowly raise and lower that arm.
fields.load: Wall angels ×8 with the low back flat. Then banded external rotation ×12, elbow tucked at your side.
fields.notice: Shoulders sit back without effort. The chest stops caving in on the lungs. Breath gets deeper on its own.
fields.careful: Do not force shoulders-back-chest-out. That retraction is the move that reproduces thoracic-outlet symptoms in people who have them — let the position come from underneath.

photos.caption: The load, standing. Yours is the same with the elbow tucked at your side. Do not force the shoulders back — that retraction is what reproduces the thoracic outlet symptoms.

items.name: Lat & back of armpit
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Lie on your side, arm overhead, ball in the back wall of the armpit. Small movements, not long rolls.
fields.load: Lat squeeze isometric — arms at your sides, squeeze the armpits down toward the hips, 5 sec ×10. Then assisted hang, feet partly down, 20–40 sec, pulling the shoulder blades DOWN.
fields.notice: Ribs stop flaring. Belly breath comes easier. Traps quieten.
fields.careful: If a shoulder subluxes or feels unstable overhead, keep the feet partly on the ground during hangs until the scapular base is solid.

photos.caption: Side-lying, arm overhead, in the back wall of the armpit. Small movements, not long rolls.

The load. Hang, then raise yourself a few inches WITHOUT bending the arms — a reverse shrug that depresses the shoulder blades. This is the "pull the blades DOWN" cue, and it is the exact drill rather than an approximation.

items.name: Mid & upper back
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Roller across the mid-back, arms crossed over the chest. A few passes, then park on a stiff segment and drape backwards over it. Breathe into it. Don't crank.
fields.load: Cat-cow ×8 with real attention to the cow — that's the direction you've lost. Then prone Y-raises ×10, light.
fields.notice: Standing tall stops being effort. Head sits back over the shoulders.
fields.careful: Extend from the mid-back, not the low back. If it hinges down low, move the roller up.

photos.caption: Roller across the mid-back, arms crossed over the chest. Park on a stiff segment and drape back over it.
Cat-cow. Give real attention to the cow direction — that is the one you have lost.

items.name: Base of skull
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.tool: Two balls in a sock, or the foam peanut
fields.release: Lie on your back and place them either side of the spine right at the base of the skull. Let the head rest into them, 3–5 min. Run slow extended-exhale breathing the whole time.
fields.load: Chin nods — lying on your back, gently nod the chin toward the throat without lifting the head. Hold 5 sec ×10. These are the deep neck flexors, the stabilizers whose absence makes the neck feel like it needs cracking.
fields.notice: The urge to crack drops. Forward-head posture is easier to correct and holds longer.
fields.careful: This replaces neck cracking. Self-manipulating the cervical spine with lax connective tissue is the one item here with a serious downside — the vertebral arteries run through the joints you would be torquing.

photos.caption: The load, seated: gentle resistance with no actual movement of the head. Yours is done lying on your back — nod the chin toward the throat without lifting the head, hold 5 seconds. Resistance, never rotation.

items.name: Front of thigh
items.why: Manual release paired with the loading that keeps it.

fields.release: Roller down the front of the thigh, weight regulated through your arms. Slow.
fields.load: Bodyweight squat to a box or chair ×10, strict form. Then step-downs ×8 each side, slow and controlled.
fields.notice: Less pull on the kneecap. The deep squat comes easier.
fields.careful: The kneeling lean-back stretch is intense on a knee in deep flexion. Keep it propped and short — or swap it for a half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with the pelvis tucked under. Same chain, far more control.

photos.caption: Roller down the front of the thigh, weight regulated through the arms. Slow.

items.name: 90/90 hip lift
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.tool: A wall, plus a rolled hand towel or a small inflatable ball — the 5–6 inch kind, like a child's playground ball — to hold between the knees
fields.notice: Low back rests flat on the floor without you holding it there. Ribs feel dropped rather than flared. This is the drill that most directly targets the anterior tilt and rib flare you identified yourself.
fields.careful: This is not a glute bridge. An inch of lift, no more. If you get lightheaded, stop and breathe normally for a minute — that is the CO2 shift, and it settles as tolerance builds.

photos.caption: Not the drill, but it shows the tilt underneath it. Yours is an inch of lift with the feet on a wall, on a long exhale.

items.name: All-fours belly lift
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.notice: You can feel your back widen on the inhale rather than your chest rising.
fields.careful: This one makes people lightheaded faster than the 90/90. Sit back on your heels if it does.

photos.caption: The belly-lift mechanic, standing: exhale everything out, then draw the navel up toward the spine and hold. Yours is the same draw on all fours with the tailbone tucked, then breathing into the BACK of the ribs.

items.name: CO2 tolerance
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.notice: Under 10 seconds is a very reactive set-point. 10–20 is reactive and common with a breathing pattern disorder. 20–30 is moderate. 40+ is well regulated. The number rising over weeks IS the thing you are trying to fix, and it is the only hard metric in this document.
fields.careful: Do it sitting or lying, never standing, given the orthostatic picture.

items.name: Extended exhale
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.notice: Tissue lets go faster under release when you are doing this than when you are not. Test it on a spot you know well.
fields.careful: If the count feels like a struggle, shorten both numbers and keep the ratio. 3 in, 5 out is fine.

items.name: Nose only, all day
items.why: Breathing is upstream of most of it. Everything else on this list is downstream effect.

fields.notice: Reaching for the mouth constantly is data, not failure — it points at nasal obstruction, which is already on your list.
fields.careful: Do not tape your mouth at night. That advice is everywhere in this space and it is specifically wrong for you: you can reproduce your own airway collapse, and taping removes the escape route.

items.name: Contract–relax
items.why: Loaded lengthening — the real answer to a nervous system guarding a range.

fields.tool: A belt, strap, towel, wall, or doorframe. Something immovable to push against
fields.notice: Range gained this way tends to still be there tomorrow. Range gained from passive holding usually is not. This is the tool for the question you actually asked.
fields.careful: 25–50% effort, not maximum. Only on restricted muscle — never used to push a joint that subluxes further into range.

photos.caption: The method itself. A partner braces the shoulders while you push your torso BACK at 25–50% for 10–20 seconds, then relax into the new range. A belt, wall or doorframe does the same job solo — the partner is just what the library had.
The starting position, not the whole method: move only to the FIRST real tension, then push against something immovable for 6–10 seconds before easing in.

items.name: Contract–relax: hamstring
items.why: Loaded lengthening — the real answer to a nervous system guarding a range.

fields.notice: Forward fold goes deeper — with soft knees, which is the version that counts.
fields.careful: Knee softly bent throughout. This drill is the safe route to the range you want; locking the knee out to gain a few degrees is the unsafe one.

photos.caption: On your back, knee softly bent. Yours uses a strap round the arch — press the heel down into it for 8 seconds, then draw the leg closer.

items.name: Contract–relax: calf
items.why: Loaded lengthening — the real answer to a nervous system guarding a range.

fields.notice: Knee-to-wall distance increases. The deep squat gets easier, because the ankle stops being the limiter.
fields.careful: If either calf has been operated on or injured, go lighter on that side.

photos.caption: Ball of the foot up the wall, heel down. Press in at 25–50%, hold 8 seconds, then lean the shin closer.
The bent-knee version, which reaches the soleus. Worth doing both — lighter on the left.

items.name: Eccentric heel drops
items.why: Loaded lengthening — the real answer to a nervous system guarding a range.

fields.tool: A step or stair with a rail
fields.notice: Calves get stronger and longer at the same time. This is how you get range that holds instead of range you have to keep re-earning.
fields.careful: Eccentrics cause real delayed soreness, and delayed is the operative word given the post-exertional picture. Start at half the volume you think you need and watch the following two days before adding any.

photos.caption: The foot position and the balance support. Yours is the edge of a stair with a rail: rise on BOTH, shift to ONE, lower that heel over a slow count of 5 well below the step, then come back up on BOTH. Never up on one leg.

items.name: Deep squat hang
items.why: Loaded lengthening — the real answer to a nervous system guarding a range.

fields.tool: A doorframe, post, or the edge of a heavy table
fields.notice: Over weeks you need less and less arm support. That is the progression — not more depth, but how much of your own weight you can hold down there.
fields.careful: Heels stay down. If they lift, the ankle is the limiter — do the calf work and take more weight through your arms in the meantime.

photos.caption: The squat pattern. Yours is a hang from a doorframe: the progression is needing less arm support, not more depth.

items.name: Between the ribs
items.why: This works what pulls on the rib cage, not the cage itself.

fields.tool: A TENNIS BALL, or your FOAM lacrosse ball. Soft. Not the firm rubber one, and not a big inflatable exercise ball
fields.notice: Side ribs expand more on the inhale. The breath feels wider rather than just deeper.
fields.careful: Light pressure only. This is bone with thin muscle strips between — a firm ball lands on the rib instead of in the gap, and you bruise easily. If it feels like pressing on bone, move the ball.

items.name: Under the rib margin
items.why: This works what pulls on the rib cage, not the cage itself.

fields.tool: Your fingers. There is no tool for this
fields.notice: Belly breath comes without effort afterwards. This is the most direct access you have to the muscle itself, and the psoas attaches into the same lumbar fascia — your best release and your main symptom are literally continuous tissue.
fields.careful: Not on a full stomach. Gentle — you are reaching under the ribs near organs, and patience works far better than pressure. Sharp pain means stop.

items.name: Side-lying rib opener
items.why: This works what pulls on the rib cage, not the cage itself.

fields.tool: Foam roller or a rolled towel
fields.notice: Rotation and side-bending get easier. Pairs naturally with the lat work.
fields.careful: Roller under the ribs, not the waist. If it presses into soft belly, move it up.

photos.caption: Side-lying with the top arm overhead. Yours adds a roller under the bottom ribs and eight breaths into the upside ribs.

items.name: Tongue posture
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.notice: You already use this deliberately as an airway compensation. The goal is making it automatic, including while asleep, which is where it would actually help the collapse.
fields.careful: Jaw tension means you are pressing with the jaw instead of the tongue. Teeth stay apart.

items.name: Tongue press & suction
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.notice: Waking less dry-mouthed. Tongue posture starting to hold without attention. Effects on sleep take months, not days — this is the slowest-acting thing in this document and also one of the highest-value.
fields.careful: Jaw fatigue is expected; jaw pain is not. Given the TMJ picture, go easy on the wide-open suction hold and cut the range right back if the joint complains.

items.name: Soft palate & throat
items.why: Myofunctional therapy. Real evidence for mild apnea and upper-airway resistance, and rarely offered.

fields.notice: Doubles as direct vagal work — the vagus nerve supplies the larynx. It is also relevant to the voice thread.
fields.careful: Nothing to speak of. This is the safest thing in the whole document.

items.name: Sciatic glide
items.why: Different tissue, different rules. Some of what reads as muscle tightness is neural.

fields.notice: If your hamstring range improves from this when stretching has not moved it, the restriction was never muscular.
fields.careful: This is flossing, not stretching — never hold the end position. If it reproduces pain, tingling, or numbness, reduce the range until it does not. More is not better here; this is one of the few drills where overdoing it clearly makes things worse.

items.name: Median nerve glide
items.why: Different tissue, different rules. Some of what reads as muscle tightness is neural.

fields.notice: Arm symptoms that come and go with position are usually neural rather than muscular. This tests that directly.
fields.careful: Given the thoracic outlet picture, start with a much smaller range than feels necessary. If it reproduces numbness or tingling, halve the range. Never push into symptoms.

photos.caption: The arm and wrist position. Yours is a GLIDE, not this held stretch — move in and out continuously, about 2 seconds each way, and never park at the end position.

items.name: Single-leg progression
items.why: Proprioception training — the direct route to knowing where your body is and what it is doing.

fields.tool: Bare feet, and a wall or counter within reach
fields.notice: Your foot will be visibly working — toes gripping, arch adjusting constantly. That is the foot-to-brain conversation you are trying to restart.
fields.careful: Stay within reach of a counter. The Level 3 head turns can trigger dizziness given the dysautonomia — if the room moves, sit down and come back to it another day at a slower speed.

photos.caption: Balance training on an unstable surface — roughly Level 4 of your progression. Levels 1–3 come first and need nothing but bare feet and a counter within reach.

items.name: Toe control
items.why: Proprioception training — the direct route to knowing where your body is and what it is doing.

fields.notice: Individual toe control is a direct readout of the nerve pathway you are trying to rebuild. Watching it go from impossible to easy is the clearest progress marker in this entire document.
fields.careful: Cramping is common at first. Stop, stretch the foot out, come back tomorrow.

items.name: Acupressure mat
items.why: Direct downregulation. Cheap, and most of it needs no equipment at all.

fields.notice: You said yourself that it helps and that you underuse it. Attach it to a fixed cue — after dinner, or while reading — rather than relying on remembering.
fields.careful: Your skin bruises and marks easily. A thin t-shirt for the first few sessions is a sensible place to start.

items.name: Humming & gargling
items.why: Direct downregulation. Cheap, and most of it needs no equipment at all.

fields.tool: Your voice, and a glass of water
fields.notice: The vagus nerve supplies the larynx, so this is about as direct as non-invasive vagal stimulation gets without a device.
fields.careful: None.

items.name: Cold on the face
items.why: Direct downregulation. Cheap, and most of it needs no equipment at all.

fields.tool: A bowl of cold water, or a cold pack
fields.notice: One of the very few things that shifts autonomic state within seconds rather than minutes.
fields.careful: Cold is a mast cell trigger for some people — test small and stop if you get flushing, itching, or hives. Not while alone if you are prone to feeling faint.

protocols.name: Full Body
protocols.notes: Hit every major muscle group in one session Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.name: Push-Up — Standard Push-Up
items.why: Chest to floor, full lockout, body in straight line

fields.release: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, body forming a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest to the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension. Keep your core tight and avoid letting your hips sag or pike up. You should feel the work in your chest, shoulders, and triceps.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, shoulders, triceps.

items.name: DB Row — Heavy Single-Arm
items.why: Flat back, pull elbow past torso, squeeze shoulder blade

fields.release: Place one hand and knee on a bench for support, keeping your back flat and parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm hanging straight down. Pull the dumbbell up by driving your elbow past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower with control. Avoid rotating your torso as you pull.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: back, biceps.

items.name: Squat — Pause Squat
items.why: Knees track over toes, hips below parallel, chest up

fields.release: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower your body as if sitting into a chair, going at least until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Romanian Deadlift — Light DB
items.why: Soft knees, hinge at hips, slide DBs along legs, flat back

fields.release: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding dumbbells in front of your thighs. With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the hips and push your butt back, sliding the dumbbells down along your legs. Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat throughout. Squeeze your glutes to drive your hips forward and return to standing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, glutes, lower back.

items.name: Plank — Standard
items.why: Straight line from head to heels, squeeze everything tight

fields.release: Get into a forearm plank position with elbows directly under shoulders and feet together or hip-width apart. Your body should form a perfectly straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your abs, glutes, and quads to maintain the position. Avoid letting your hips sag toward the floor or pike upward. Breathe steadily throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, obliques, shoulders.

items.name: Bear Crawl — Forward/Back
items.why: Knees hover off floor, opposite hand and foot move together

fields.release: Start on all fours and lift your knees just one to two inches off the floor. Crawl forward by moving the opposite hand and foot together (right hand with left foot, then left hand with right foot). Keep your back flat and your knees hovering low. Avoid letting your hips rock side to side. This builds core stability, shoulder endurance, and coordination.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core, quads.

protocols.name: Upper Body
protocols.notes: Push and pull balance for upper body strength Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.why: Chest to floor, full lockout, body in straight line

fields.release: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, body forming a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest to the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension. Keep your core tight and avoid letting your hips sag or pike up. You should feel the work in your chest, shoulders, and triceps.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, shoulders, triceps.

items.name: DB Row — Heavy Single-Arm
items.why: Flat back, pull elbow past torso, squeeze shoulder blade

fields.release: Place one hand and knee on a bench for support, keeping your back flat and parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm hanging straight down. Pull the dumbbell up by driving your elbow past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower with control. Avoid rotating your torso as you pull.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: back, biceps.

items.name: Dip — Legs Extended Dip
items.why: Lean slightly forward, elbows back, full depth

fields.release: Place your hands on parallel bars or the edge of a sturdy bench behind you and support your body weight with arms extended. Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, then press back up to lockout. Lean your torso slightly forward to emphasize your chest, or stay upright to target triceps more. Avoid shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, triceps, shoulders.

items.name: Lateral Raise — Light DB
items.why: Slight bend in elbows, raise to shoulder height, control down

fields.release: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower slowly. Avoid swinging or using momentum, and do not raise above shoulder level. You should feel this in the sides of your shoulders.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders.

items.name: DB Curl — Moderate
items.why: Elbows pinned, supinate at top, no swinging

fields.release: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended at your sides with palms facing forward. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows, squeezing your biceps at the top, then lower slowly. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging your body to generate momentum.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: biceps.

items.name: Mountain Climber — Standard
items.why: Plank position, drive knees to chest, hips low and stable

fields.release: Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders. Rapidly drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs in a running motion while keeping your hips low and stable. Avoid letting your hips bounce up and down. The faster you go, the more cardiovascular demand. Keep your core braced to maintain a flat back throughout.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: abs, hip flexors.

protocols.name: Lower Body
protocols.notes: Quads, hamstrings, glutes, and calves Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.name: Squat — Pause Squat
items.why: Knees track over toes, hips below parallel, chest up

fields.release: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward. Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower your body as if sitting into a chair, going at least until your thighs are parallel to the floor. Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes. Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Lunge — Reverse Lunge
items.why: Long step, knee hovers above floor, drive through front heel

fields.release: Stand tall and take a long step forward. Lower your body by bending both knees until your rear knee hovers just above the floor and your front thigh is roughly parallel to the ground. Drive through your front heel to return to standing. Keep your torso upright throughout and avoid letting your front knee shoot past your toes.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: quads, glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Romanian Deadlift — Light DB
items.why: Soft knees, hinge at hips, slide DBs along legs, flat back

fields.release: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding dumbbells in front of your thighs. With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at the hips and push your butt back, sliding the dumbbells down along your legs. Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings, keeping your back flat throughout. Squeeze your glutes to drive your hips forward and return to standing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hamstrings, glutes, lower back.

items.name: Glute Bridge — Single-Leg
items.why: Drive hips up, squeeze glutes hard at top, feet flat

fields.release: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. Drive through your heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling, squeezing your glutes as hard as you can at the top. Lower your hips back down with control. Avoid pushing from your lower back; the movement should come from your glutes. You should feel a strong contraction in your glutes at the top.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, hamstrings.

items.name: Calf Raise — Single-Leg
items.why: Full stretch at bottom, high on toes at top, slow tempo

fields.release: Stand with feet hip-width apart, ideally with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step so your heels can drop below for a full stretch. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing your calves at the top, then lower slowly below the step level. Use a slow, controlled tempo and avoid bouncing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: calves.

items.name: Banded Crab Walk — Medium
items.why: Band above knees, quarter squat, step laterally with tension

fields.release: Place a resistance band just above your knees and stand in a quarter-squat position with feet hip-width apart. Step sideways with one foot, maintaining tension in the band, then follow with the other foot. Keep your hips low and your knees pushed outward against the band. You should feel this in your outer glutes and hip abductors.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, hip abductors.

protocols.name: Push Day
protocols.notes: Chest, shoulders, and triceps focus Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.name: Push-Up — Standard Push-Up
items.why: Chest to floor, full lockout, body in straight line

fields.release: Start in a plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, body forming a straight line from head to heels. Lower your chest to the floor by bending your elbows, then press back up to full arm extension. Keep your core tight and avoid letting your hips sag or pike up. You should feel the work in your chest, shoulders, and triceps.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, shoulders, triceps.

items.name: Dip — Legs Extended Dip
items.why: Lean slightly forward, elbows back, full depth

fields.release: Place your hands on parallel bars or the edge of a sturdy bench behind you and support your body weight with arms extended. Lower yourself by bending your elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, then press back up to lockout. Lean your torso slightly forward to emphasize your chest, or stay upright to target triceps more. Avoid shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: chest, triceps, shoulders.

items.name: DB Overhead Press — Seated Moderate
items.why: Brace core, press straight overhead, full lockout

fields.release: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with palms facing forward. Brace your core and press both dumbbells straight overhead until your arms are fully extended. Lower them back to shoulder height with control. Avoid arching your lower back excessively; if you find yourself leaning back, reduce the weight.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, triceps.

items.name: Lateral Raise — Light DB
items.why: Slight bend in elbows, raise to shoulder height, control down

fields.release: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. With a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower slowly. Avoid swinging or using momentum, and do not raise above shoulder level. You should feel this in the sides of your shoulders.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders.

items.name: DB Tricep Extension — Single-Arm Overhead
items.why: Keep elbows close to head, full stretch and lockout

fields.release: Stand or sit and hold a dumbbell overhead with both hands or one hand. Keeping your upper arm vertical and elbow pointed at the ceiling, lower the weight behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in the triceps. Extend your arm back to full lockout. Avoid flaring your elbows outward or arching your back.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: triceps.

items.name: Shoulder Tap — Standard Plank Tap
items.why: Minimize hip rotation, keep hips square to floor

fields.release: Start in a high plank position with hands directly under shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width apart. Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder, then return it to the floor and repeat on the other side. The key challenge is keeping your hips perfectly still and square to the floor; widen your stance to make this easier.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: shoulders, core.

protocols.name: Pull Day
protocols.notes: Back, biceps, and rear delts Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.name: DB Row — Heavy Single-Arm
items.why: Flat back, pull elbow past torso, squeeze shoulder blade

fields.release: Place one hand and knee on a bench for support, keeping your back flat and parallel to the floor. Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm hanging straight down. Pull the dumbbell up by driving your elbow past your torso and squeezing your shoulder blade toward your spine, then lower with control. Avoid rotating your torso as you pull.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: back, biceps.

items.name: Banded Lat Pulldown — Medium
items.why: Anchor band high, pull elbows to ribs, squeeze lats

fields.release: Anchor a resistance band at a high point above you. Kneel or stand facing the anchor and grab both ends of the band with arms extended overhead. Pull your elbows down to your ribs, squeezing your lats hard at the bottom, then slowly extend your arms back up. Think about driving your elbows into your back pockets.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lats, biceps.

items.name: DB Curl — Moderate
items.why: Elbows pinned, supinate at top, no swinging

fields.release: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, arms fully extended at your sides with palms facing forward. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders by bending at the elbows, squeezing your biceps at the top, then lower slowly. Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and avoid swinging your body to generate momentum.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: biceps.

items.name: Banded Face Pull — Heavy
items.why: Pull band to face, elbows high, squeeze rear delts

fields.release: Anchor a resistance band at about face height. Hold both ends and step back to create tension. Pull the band toward your face with elbows high and wide, squeezing your rear deltoids and upper back at the end position. Return slowly. This exercise is excellent for posture and shoulder health.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: rear delts, upper back.

items.name: Superman — Pulse
items.why: Lift arms and legs off floor, squeeze glutes and back

fields.release: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight. Simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor by squeezing your glutes and lower back muscles. Hold briefly at the top, then lower with control. Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor rather than cranking your head up.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: lower back, glutes.

items.name: Farmer's Carry — Moderate
items.why: Shoulders packed, chest tall, walk with purpose

fields.release: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand and stand tall with your shoulders pulled down and back (packed). Walk forward in a controlled manner, keeping your chest up and core braced. Avoid leaning to either side. This builds grip strength, trap endurance, and core stability. Walk until your grip gives out or you reach your target distance.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: forearms, traps, core.

protocols.name: Mobility Flow
protocols.notes: Hip, ankle, shoulder, and spine mobility Switch this on for the days you are doing it.

items.name: World's Greatest Stretch — With Rotation
items.why: Lunge, plant hand, rotate and reach to sky, feel every part open

fields.release: Step into a deep lunge position and plant the hand on the same side as your front foot on the floor inside the foot. Rotate your torso and reach the other arm toward the sky, opening your chest. Hold briefly, then return your hand to the floor. This stretch hits the hips, hamstrings, thoracic spine, and groin all in one movement.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hips, thoracic, hamstrings.

items.name: Deep Squat Hold — Unassisted 30s
items.why: Sit deep, heels down, chest up, breathe and relax into it

fields.release: Lower yourself into the deepest squat position you can while keeping your heels on the floor. Hold the position, keeping your chest upright and breathing deeply to relax into the stretch. If your heels rise, widen your stance or hold onto a support. This opens up the hips, ankles, and thoracic spine. Aim to accumulate time rather than rushing.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hips, ankles, thoracic.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switch — Elevated Hands
items.why: Both knees at 90 degrees, switch sides by rotating hips

fields.release: Sit on the floor with both knees bent at 90 degrees, one leg in front and one behind, creating a "90/90" position. Rotate your hips to switch both legs to the other side so the front leg becomes the back leg and vice versa. Keep your chest tall throughout. This exercise mobilizes the hips through internal and external rotation.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hip internal/external rotation.

items.name: Hip CARs — Freestanding
items.why: Slow controlled circles at the hip, biggest circle possible

fields.release: Stand on one leg or kneel on all fours. Lift one knee and slowly draw the biggest circle possible with your hip joint, moving through flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction. Make smooth, controlled circles in both directions. This maintains hip joint range of motion and highlights any areas of tightness.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: hips.

items.name: Thoracic Spine Rotation — Windmill
items.why: Lock hips, rotate through upper back only, reach and open

fields.release: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked. Keeping your hips locked in place, rotate your upper back to open your top arm toward the floor on the other side. Return to the starting position. The key is isolating the rotation to your thoracic spine while your hips stay still. This is especially beneficial if you sit for long periods.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: thoracic spine.

items.name: Pigeon Stretch — Forward Fold
items.why: Front shin across body, square hips, ease into stretch

fields.release: From a kneeling position, bring one shin across your body in front of you with the knee angled outward. Extend your other leg straight behind you. Square your hips toward the front and ease your torso down toward the floor. You should feel a deep stretch in the front hip and glute. Use your hands for support and breathe into the stretch.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: glutes, hip flexors.

items.name: Banded Ankle Dorsiflexion — Medium
items.why: Band pulls ankle back, drive knee forward over toes

fields.release: Anchor a resistance band low and loop it around the front of your ankle. Face away from the anchor point in a half-kneeling position. The band pulls your ankle backward, creating a distraction force. Drive your knee forward over your toes against the band resistance. This improves ankle dorsiflexion, which is crucial for squatting depth and athletic performance.
fields.notice: Where the work should land: tibialis anterior, ankles.
